title: Throughput Thermostat: adaptive token-rate microprobe for core LLMs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build and maintain an adaptive microbenchmark (the 'Throughput Thermostat') that measures tokens-per-second and p95 latency for core serving models under realistic burst and drift patterns. The harness should simulate prefix/KV cache states, vary sequence lengths, and run short-lived scenarios that reliably surface regressions in throughput and p95. Results must feed into CI alerts and a console dashboard for trending.
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness can run against a specified model version and return mean tokens/sec and p50/p95/p99 latencies within 15 minutes
Synthetic burst generator supports Poisson and stepped-burst profiles and can replay prefix corpus to simulate KV cache warmup
Automated regression detector emits a CI-failing signal when p95 increases by >10% or tokens/sec drops by >7% compared to baseline with configurable sensitivity
Benchmark outputs are stored to metrics DB and a per-model dashboard is created in Console showing 30d trend and recent raw runs
Baseline suite includes at least 3 core models and runs in the nightly perf job with per-model histograms and sample traces
design_decisions: Use an adaptive load phase (thermostat) that drives token rate up until target latency bound is reached, then backs off to measure sustainable throughput
Prefer non-parametric change detection (Mann-Whitney U + bootstrap of medians) for p95 drift, avoid strict Gaussian assumptions
Simulate KV cache by replaying a short corpus of recent real inference prefixes captured (anonymized) from production to avoid unrealistic cold-cache tests
Keep single-run duration short (8-12 minutes) so CI integration is feasible; aggregate 6 runs per model for stability
Store both summary metrics and raw token-level timestamps to enable post-hoc tomography and p95 reconstruction
tradeoffs: Synthetic prompts are faster to iterate but may miss distributional artifacts; decided to mix synthetic and replayed short prefixes
Tighter statistical tests increase false positives in noisy environments; selected conservative thresholds and allow auto-tuning per-model
Adding KV warmup increases test runtime; to compensate we cap warmup to 30s of realistic prefixes per run
Targeting CI breakout on regressions increases alert fatigue; added a secondary triage job that runs longer diagnostics before paging
implementation_plan: 1) Implement burst profile generator and thermostat loop as a Python binary with pluggable transport (REST / internal RPC)
2) Integrate prefix replay module that reads anonymized prefix bundles from S3 and warms model KV cache prior to measurement
3) Add result serializer to push summaries to metrics DB and raw traces to object store
4) Implement regression detector microservice that compares new runs to rolling baseline and emits CI annotations and Slack alerts
5) Wire nightly perf job to run the suite across selected GPUs and publish dashboards
6) Add CLI and GitHub Actions step so PRs that touch the runtime can run a lightweight smoke measurement
test_plan: Unit tests for thermostat controller, burst generator, and prefix player
Synthetic validation: inject an artificial 12% tokenization slowdown and verify regression detector flags it in <= 2 runs
Integration: run suite against staging model cluster and validate metrics ingestion and dashboard rendering
Longer soak: weekly extended-run mode (2h) that exercises KV eviction and multi-context steady-state throughput
A/B canary: compare new model variant against baseline with paired-run statistical test before rollout
